stage.name: Sakaide to Sanuki
stage.theme: The longest day of the forty, and the most crowded
stage.narrative: 59.6 km, the longest day of the forty this cut made, and it is long for an absence: from 63.8 km to 149.9 km — 86.1 km — this section's record marks no place to stay at all, and this day is 59.6 of that stretch. No town falls in it either, until the one it ends at. What the day is not is empty. A hundred and sixty-three of Sanuki's three hundred and eighty-nine recorded places stand on it, nearly twice the next day's count, and the longest run with nothing marked on it is only 4.2 km. Seven temples come among them — Tennō-ji, Sanuki Kokubun-ji, Shiromine-ji, Negoro-ji, Ichinomiya-ji, Yashima-ji and Yakuri-ji — with forty-two bus stops, thirty-one places to eat and sixteen convenience stores. Everything except somewhere to stop.
stage.closing: The busiest day in Sanuki and the longest of the forty, and those are one fact: nothing recorded on it is a place to sleep. How much of what you carry is decided by what someone wrote down?
warnings: 59.6 km, the longest day on the circuit. OpenStreetMap records no named accommodation or town on the walked line between Sakaide and Sanuki, so the rule had nowhere nearer to stop. Carry water and food for the whole distance, or break the day at a place off the line.
